In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hydrogenic retention in high-Z materials is low for high-temperature, low-density plasma conditions.

the retention of hydrogenic species in the form of deuterium on the surface of W and Mo targets exposed to the conditions expected in the ITER divertor is very low, with the retained fraction of Dretained/D incident ranging from 10 −8 to 10 −5.
plasma flux is not a major factor for hydrogenic retention in high-Z materials at the temperatures and plasma fluxes relevant for ITER.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hydrogenic retention of high-temperature refractory metals in the ITER divertor can be low, even for the highest flux densities and highest plasma temperatures.
the surface temperature is the key parameter for determining retention in W and the retention in Mo is similar but slightly higher due to lower surface temperatures.
hydrogenic retention of W and Mo in a detached divertor plasma is very low and is not expected to be a major concern for ITER.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the retention of high-temperature refractory metals exposed under ITER divertor-relevant plasma conditions is low and is not strongly influenced by incident flux.
hydrogenic retention is strongly influenced in the surface temperature range of 800–16000 K, which is the range expected at the ITER divertor strike point.
the retention of high-Z refractory metals exposed at the strike point is expected to be low, and thus these metals can be considered as a viable option for the ITER divertor.
